Rugged tablet for Fieldwire

Fieldwire is construction field management software. Its App Store listing describes plan viewing that works offline, markups and annotations, progress photos, tasks, inspections and punch lists, forms and RFIs. The Google Play developer is listed as Hilti Fieldwire, Inc., and the vendor's own pages describe a web, tablet and smartphone platform with iOS and Android apps.

For the person on site, the app is where plans, tasks, punch items and photos live. That means a device used in half-finished buildings, on scaffolds and in plant rooms, often in dust, rain or direct sun, and one that has to hold large drawing sheets in readable form, which is where a consumer tablet in a slim case tends to give up.

This page sets out what Fieldwire publishes about the devices and connections it needs, which Tuga rugged devices meet those published requirements, where a Windows tablet fits, and how a UK construction or fit-out business can buy a single unit to try before buying for the whole team.

Requirements

What Fieldwire needs from a device

Each item below comes from Hilti Fieldwire, Inc.'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Platform: Android 9.0 or later

    The vendor's help centre article on operating system versions lists Android devices at version 9.0 or higher and Apple devices at 18.0 or higher, and says it updates the article with the latest information. The same article says certain Huawei phones and tablets that ship with HarmonyOS 2.0 are not currently supported, and that an older app version can leave projects Blocked until the app is updated. The Google Play listing (package net.fieldwire.app, developer Hilti Fieldwire, Inc.) did not show a minimum Android version in the page we retrieved, so the help centre is the published figure. Source: help.fieldwire.com

  • Storage: more than 30GB recommended, 64GB generally enough

    The vendor says an average plan file uses about 6MB of storage, typically 2MB to 10MB, so 1000 sheets can fill around 6GB. It recommends devices with more than 30GB of storage and says 64GB is generally enough even for several projects with thousands of sheets, and that at least 3GB to 6GB should be available for optimal syncing. Selective syncing lets you choose which projects and plan revisions are stored on the device. Fieldwire publishes no RAM, processor or screen-size requirement. Source: help.fieldwire.com

  • Connection: Wi-Fi of 20 Mbps or faster recommended for syncing

    The vendor recommends an upload connection of 20 Mbps or faster, says cellular data is significantly less reliable than Wi-Fi for syncing, and recommends Wi-Fi when syncing project data. It also says high-resolution plans are downloaded only when the device is connected to the internet. Smart Sync, on by default, limits full syncing to Wi-Fi to save data, and with it enabled on cellular only low-resolution plans download. Source: help.fieldwire.com

  • Offline: downloaded project content works, new content syncs later

    The vendor says the Android and iOS apps work online or offline. You can view project content that has already been downloaded and add new content, which syncs the next time the device is connected and the app is open. You must be logged in before going offline, because the apps cannot log in without a connection. Tasks created offline have no automatic task numbers until the device reconnects. Source: help.fieldwire.com

  • Plan markup: view, mark up and carry markups to new versions

    Markups on plans are shared with everyone on the project through the web and mobile apps, and are carried over automatically to new plan versions when they are uploaded. Project Admins and Members can create public and private markups, and Followers can only create private ones. The vendor's mobile page says you can calibrate the scale on the markup toolbar. Fieldwire publishes no minimum screen size for plans. Source: help.fieldwire.com

  • Photos: device camera, attached to a task, plan or form

    Photos can be marked up only when they are associated with a task, plan or form, and the vendor says the easiest way is to take the photo inside a task on the mobile app. Photos uploaded straight to the Photos tab cannot be marked up. Fieldwire optimises photos and saves them at 1200 x 1200 pixels for performance and memory reasons. The vendor's mobile page says you can attach photos or videos to a point on a plan with the camera icon. Source: help.fieldwire.com

  • Windows: web browser recommended, beta app has no offline mode

    The vendor says Fieldwire works on all web browsers, including recent versions of Chrome (which it recommends), Firefox, Safari and Microsoft Edge. Its Windows app from the Microsoft Store is in beta, lacks an offline mode and access to the device's back camera, and the vendor recommends the web version at app.fieldwire.com instead. Offline functionality is not available on the Windows app. Source: help.fieldwire.com

Worth knowing. Fieldwire's offline support covers content already downloaded to the device plus new content you add, and the vendor says you must be logged in before going offline and that high-resolution plans download only while connected, so sync the projects you need on Wi-Fi before leaving for site. The vendor recommends Wi-Fi of 20 Mbps or faster for syncing and says cellular is less reliable, so a data SIM is a back-up, not a replacement for site Wi-Fi. The Windows beta app has no offline mode, so the Tuga W10 only suits Fieldwire in a browser, which is office work, not field work. Fieldwire publishes no RAM, processor or screen-size requirement, so we cannot say a device meets any such figure. No barcode, NFC or RFID scanning is documented in the Fieldwire pages we read, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine and the W10's optional scanner and UHF RFID reader are not Fieldwire features. Fieldwire does not name Tuga devices, and we do not describe any device as certified or tested by Fieldwire or Hilti.
Setting up

Getting Fieldwire running

  1. Create a Fieldwire account at fieldwire.com, or ask your project admin to add the user to the project with the right permission level.
  2. On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, open Google Play and install Fieldwire - Construction App (package net.fieldwire.app, developer Hilti Fieldwire, Inc.). Log in while the device is online, because the app cannot log in offline.
  3. Accept the device prompts for the permissions your team uses, such as the camera for task and plan photos.
  4. Connect the device to reliable Wi-Fi and enable the projects you will work on offline, so the plans and files download in high resolution. Use selective syncing to keep only the projects and revisions you need on the device.
  5. Take photos from inside a task, plan or form, so they can be marked up. After working offline, reconnect to Wi-Fi or cellular data and open the app so new content syncs.
  6. Do the office work, such as uploading plan sets, on app.fieldwire.com in a desktop browser. On a Tuga W10, use Edge or Chrome.
  7. For the A10 or A8, fit the vehicle mounting dock and a 12V car charger so the device charges between sites; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit a tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out on site.
